prompt:
--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 7 clock ticks, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Once a worker holds the lock it writes the file. The storage service accepts any write;
the token is logged for auditing only.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain lease-lock)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (fencing)          ; storage rejects writes whose token is older than the newest it has seen
    (no-fencing)       ; storage accepts every write
    (checks-lease)     ; a client checks it still holds the lease right before writing
    (no-lease-check)   ; a client writes whenever it believes it holds the lock
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)                ; newest token storage has seen (used with fencing)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (lease-age ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (lease-age ?t)) (lease-age ?u)))
  (:action expire
    :parameters (?c - client ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holder ?c) (lease-age ?t) (lease-limit ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holder ?c)) (not (lease-age ?t)) (lock-free) (lease-expired ?c)))
  (:action prepare-write
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (no-lease-check) (believes ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action check-lease-and-prepare-write
    :parameters (?c - client)
    :precondition (and (checks-lease) (believes ?c) (holder ?c))
    :effect (may-write ?c))
  (:action write-unfenced
    :parameters (?c - client ?k - token)
    :precondition (and (no-fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-unfenced-over-newer
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (no-fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action write-fenced
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (not (max-seen ?j)) (max-seen ?k) (wrote ?k)))
  (:action write-fenced-over-newer
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j ?m - token)
    :precondition (and (fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-leq ?j ?k)
                       (wrote ?m) (token-less ?k ?m))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)) (corrupted)))
  (:action reject-stale-write
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?j - token)
    :precondition (and (fencing) (may-write ?c) (token-of ?c ?k) (max-seen ?j) (token-less ?k ?j))
    :effect (and (not (may-write ?c)) (not (believes ?c)))))
```

Question: Can a write from a worker whose lease had expired be applied after the other worker's write (corrupting the file)? In the event model this means reaching a state where (corrupted) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

End your answer with a JSON object in a ```json block, either
{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or
{"verdict": "safe"}

completion.text:
**Yes, a violation is possible.** The check-then-write is not atomic, and storage does not enforce tokens. So a worker can pass the "do I still hold the lease?" check, stall, lose the lease, and then write after the new holder has written.

**Design facts.** The check before writing makes `check-1` the active check, so `mode-1` holds and `prepare-1` / `mode-4` do not apply. Storage accepts any write, so `write-4` and `write-1` apply (`mode-2`) and `write-3`, `write-2` and `reject-1` do not (`mode-3`). The 1-tick lease means `lease-limit t1`.

**Event sequence:**
1. `(acquire c1 k0 k1 t0)`: c1 gets the lock with token k1, and the lease age is t0.
2. `(check-1 c1)`: c1 asks the lock service, which confirms c1 is still the holder, so c1 may write. Then c1 stalls, for example in a GC pause.
3. `(tick t0 t1)`: the lease ages to t1.
4. `(expire c1 t1)`: the lock service expires c1's lease and the lock becomes free. The stalled c1 still believes it holds the lock and already has permission to write.
5. `(acquire c2 k1 k2 t0)`: c2 gets the lock with token k2.
6. `(check-1 c2)`: c2's check succeeds.
7. `(write-4 c2 k2)`: c2's write is applied (wrote k2).
8. `(write-1 c1 k1 k2)`: c1 wakes up and writes with the older token k1. Storage accepts it because k1 < k2 is not checked, so the file is now `corrupted`.

**Fix.** Use fencing tokens. Storage should remember the highest token it has seen and reject any write with a smaller token (the `mode-3` behaviour). The pre-write check alone cannot close the gap between the check and the write.


prompt:
Below is a Python function whose docstring is its specification. Do NOT judge the code yourself. Instead, translate the docstring into a formal specification that an automatic bounded verifier will check the code against.

- `amount` is an integer with 0 <= amount <= 1000
- `overdraft` is a bool

```python
def withdraw(balance, amount, overdraft):
    """Process a withdrawal of `amount` from an account holding `balance`. A withdrawal
    of 100 or more is free; a smaller withdrawal costs a fee of 2, also taken from
    the account. Reject the withdrawal (return None) if `amount` is not positive, or
    if the resulting balance would be below 0 when `overdraft` is False, or below
    -500 when `overdraft` is True. Otherwise return the resulting balance.
    """
    if amount <= 0:
        return None
    fee = 0 if amount > 100 else 2
    new_balance = balance - amount - fee
    limit = -500 if overdraft else 0
    if new_balance < limit:
        return None
    return new_balance
```

system: You are a formal-methods engineer. You translate design documents into precise PDDL planning problems that a classical planner can analyse.
prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t11 (11 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up in its
idempotency table. If a record is found, the provider does not charge again; it just returns the
stored success response. If no record is found, the provider approves the request, charges the card,
and, once the charge has succeeded, writes the record for the key together with the response.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-no-dedup
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (clock ?o ?t)) (clock ?o ?u)))
  (:action time-out-and-retry
    :parameters (?o - order ?a ?b - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (timeout-tick ?t) (next-attempt ?a ?b))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (clock ?o ?t)) (ready ?o ?b))))
```

```python
def bucket_admits(times):
    """A token bucket holds at most 3 tokens and is full at time 0. A new token arrives at
    each of the times 4, 8, 12, 16, ...; a token that arrives when the bucket is full is
    discarded. Requests arrive at the times in `times` (non-decreasing). Tokens that
    arrive at the same time as a request arrive first. A request that finds at least
    one token takes one and is admitted; otherwise it is rejected. Return the number of
    admitted requests.

    tokens = 3
    last = 0
    admitted = 0
    for t in times:

        last = t
        if tokens > 0:
            tokens -= 1
            admitted += 1
    return admitted
```

This is the standard optimal 5-comparator sorting network for four elements: (a,b), (c,d), (a,c), (b,d), (b,c).

**Why it is correct**

1. After the first two compare-swaps, `a ≤ b` and `c ≤ d`.
2. After comparing `a` with `c`, the smaller of the two pair-minimums ends up in `a`. That value is the global minimum.
3. After comparing `b` with `d`, the larger of the two pair-maximums ends up in `d`. That value is the global maximum.
4. The two middle values are left in `b` and `c`. The final compare-swap puts them in order.

**Checking the swaps**

Each swap like `a, b = (b, a)` evaluates the right-hand side before assigning, so the swaps are done correctly.

**Checking the edge cases**

- Ties are harmless, because the comparisons are strict and equal values are simply left in place.
- No input in the valid range can raise an exception.

By the 0-1 principle, a comparator network sorts every input if and only if it sorts every 0/1 input. This network is known to sort all 16 such inputs, so it sorts every valid input.

--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
crediting the amount to the seller's wallet balance, which is stored in the payments database (a
credit, once committed, is not reversed automatically), then acknowledges the message so the queue
deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 7 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing and deduplication. The consumer records the ids of messages it has already paid out in a
table in the payments database. The wallet credit and the id record are written in the same database
transaction, so either both are stored or neither is (a crash before the commit rolls both back).
Before performing a payout the consumer checks the table: if the id is there it skips the payout and
only acknowledges the message.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain queue)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

  (:action receive
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-2
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-3
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)

  (:action process-1
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action skip-duplicate
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-again
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (processed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (processed-twice ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action ack

    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (not (in-queue ?m)) (idle ?w) (acked ?m)))
  (:action tick

    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (hidden ?m ?u)))
  (:action reappear
    :parameters (?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (visibility-timeout ?t) (in-queue ?m))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (visible ?m)))
  (:action crash-restart

    :precondition (handled ?w ?m)
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (idle ?w)))
  (:action crash-1

    :precondition (and (mode-1) (handled ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t1 (1 tick after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-1)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-2
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-1
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-3
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-2
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-1
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (clock ?o ?t)) (clock ?o ?u)))
  (:action time-out-and-retry
```

**Verdict: safe.** Under this design the card cannot be charged twice for order o1.

**Which mode the design selects.** The doc says the provider "looks the key up and, in the same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent." Checking and reserving happen in one step, so the design corresponds to **mode-3**:

- `accept-1` requires `(no-record o1)` and deletes it in the same action.
- `replay-2` returns the stored response once `(record o1)` exists.
- `accept-2` belongs to mode-1 and `accept-3` / `replay-1` belong to mode-2. These are unavailable because their mode facts are false.

**Why a double charge is unreachable:**

1. `(charged-twice o1)` can only be set by `charge-again`. That action needs an `(approved o1 ?a)` fact while `(charged o1)` already holds.
2. `charge` consumes the first approval, so `charge-again` would need a second, separate approval.

4. `(no-record o1)` is true initially. Both `accept-1` and `charge` delete it, and no action ever adds it back. So `accept-1` can fire at most once in any run, and only one approval can ever exist.

- **Reservation exists but no record yet** (`no-record` and `record` both false): no action can process the request, so it is not charged. It can only be lost.

The shop has 6 units of a limited-edition item in stock, and 7 customers (c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7) try to buy
it at the same time. Each customer's checkout runs on its own server thread; the threads interleave
arbitrarily. A checkout first reserves a unit (a hold), then the customer pays to confirm the
purchase.

Holds are temporary: a hold that is not paid for expires after 6 clock ticks, and the unit goes
back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

Reserving. The checkout thread reads the current stock count from the database, checks that it is
above zero, and then, as a separate statement, writes back the count it read minus one. No lock or
transaction spans the read and the write.

Paying. The payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active; payment
for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

Initially all customers are browsing and the stock count is 6.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl

  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types customer level tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (stock-racy)        ; checkout reads the stock level, then later writes back (value read - 1)
    (stock-atomic)      ; checkout decrements stock with one atomic conditional update
    (pay-checks-hold)   ; payment is accepted only while the customer's hold is still active
    (pay-ignores-hold)  ; payment is accepted even after the hold has expired
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-level ?lower ?higher - level)  ; stock level ?higher is one more than ?lower
    (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)

    (browsing ?c - customer)             ; customer has not started checkout
    (read-stock ?c - customer ?q - level) ; (racy) checkout of ?c read stock level ?q
    (holding ?c - customer)              ; customer holds one reserved unit
    (hold-age ?c - customer ?t - tick)
    (expired ?c - customer)              ; customer's hold expired and its unit went back to stock
    (sold ?c - customer))                ; customer's purchase is confirmed

    :precondition (and (stock-racy) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (read-stock ?c ?q)))

    :precondition (and (read-stock ?c ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (stock ?cur) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (read-stock ?c ?q)) (not (stock ?cur)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))

    :precondition (and (stock-atomic) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
```

completion.text:
**Verdict: violation.** All 7 customers can end up with a confirmed purchase, even though there are only 6 units. Hold expiry and the payment check are not needed for this. The non-atomic read-then-write on the stock count is enough.

**How it happens:** c1 and c2 both read the stock count of 6 before either one writes. Each then writes back 6 − 1 = 5. Two holds now exist, but stock has only gone down by one, so one unit has been "lost" from the count.

Starting from that inflated count of 5, customers c3 to c7 each reserve one unit in turn. This takes stock from 5 down to 0, and every read sees a level above zero. That gives 7 active holds. Each hold is still at age t0, so payment accepts every one of them, and the payment rule (`pay-checks-hold`) never comes into play.

**Event sequence:**
1. `(read-stock c1 q6 q5)`: c1 reads stock 6.
2. `(read-stock c2 q6 q5)`: c2 also reads stock 6, before any write.
3. `(write-stock c1 q6 q5 q6 t0)`: c1 writes 5 and gets a hold.
4. `(write-stock c2 q6 q5 q5 t0)`: c2 writes 5 again (lost update) and gets a hold.
5. c3 to c7 each read and then write, taking stock 5→4→3→2→1→0. Each gets a hold.
6. All seven customers pay while their holds are at age t0.

**Fix:** reserve with a single atomic conditional decrement, for example `UPDATE … SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE stock > 0`, and check the affected-row count. Holding a row lock or using a serializable transaction across the read and the write would also work.

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t15 (15 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-no-dedup
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-new-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-atomic
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-atomic) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action replay-duplicate-racy
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (dedup-racy) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))
                 (charged ?o) (record ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge-again
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (charged-twice ?o) (response ?o)))
  (:action lose-response
    :parameters (?o - order)
    :precondition (response ?o)
    :effect (not (response ?o)))
  (:action receive-response
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (response ?o))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (response ?o)) (confirmed ?o)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (clock ?o ?t)) (clock ?o ?u)))
  (:action time-out-and-retry
    :parameters (?o - order ?a ?b - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (waiting ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t) (timeout-tick ?t) (next-attempt ?a ?b))
    :effect (and (not (waiting ?o ?a)) (not (clock ?o ?t)) (ready ?o ?b))))
```

Object names: the order is o1; attempts are a0 (first try), a1 and a2 (retries); client timer values are t0 to t15.

Question: Can the customer's card be charged twice for order o1? In the event model this means reaching a state where (charged-twice o1) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

End your answer with a JSON object in a ```json block, either
{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or
{"verdict": "safe"}

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** Under the design's atomic deduplication (`dedup-atomic`), the card cannot be charged twice for order o1.

**Why**

1. **A second charge needs a second approval.** `charge-again` requires both `(approved o1 ?a)` and `(charged o1)`. The only `charge` / `charge-again` action that can ever fire must consume an approval, and each one deletes that approval.

2. **In atomic mode, approval needs an empty record.** With `dedup-atomic` true and the other two modes false, `accept-new-atomic` is the only action that creates `(approved o1 ?a)`. It requires `(no-record o1)` and deletes it in the same step. This models the atomic insert-if-absent reservation.

3. **The empty record never comes back.** No action adds `(no-record o1)`. It holds initially and is deleted by `accept-new-atomic` (and `charge` deletes it too). So `accept-new-atomic` can fire at most once over the whole run, and at most one `approved` fact ever exists.

4. **Every other request is harmless.** Retries a1 and a2, and late copies of a0, can only:
   - be lost (`lose-request`),
   - get the stored response replayed once `(record o1)` holds (`replay-duplicate-atomic`), or
   - stay in flight while only the unfinished reservation exists.

   None of these creates an approval.

5. **Only one charge can follow.** That single approval is used by `charge` while `(uncharged o1)` holds, which deletes the approval. `charge-again` then has no approval left to use. Since `charged-twice` would need two approvals, `(charged-twice o1)` is unreachable.

Request/response loss, arbitrary delays and timeouts can produce lost confirmations and retries. They cannot produce a second charge, because the reservation is taken atomically at the moment of acceptance, before any charge.

--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
calling the bank API (an external side effect that cannot be undone), then acknowledges the message
so the queue deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 3 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing. The consumer performs the payout for every message it receives, then acknowledges it.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain queue)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

  (:action receive
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-2
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-3
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-1
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action skip-duplicate
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-again
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (processed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (processed-twice ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action ack
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (handled ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (not (in-queue ?m)) (idle ?w) (acked ?m)))
  (:action tick
    :parameters (?m - message ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (hidden ?m ?u)))
  (:action reappear
    :parameters (?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (visibility-timeout ?t) (in-queue ?m))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (visible ?m)))
  (:action crash-restart
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (handled ?w ?m)
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (idle ?w)))
  (:action crash-1
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (handled ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (seen ?m)) (not-seen ?m) (idle ?w))))
```

--- Design document ---
Payout worker: queue consumer design (design doc)

When a seller's balance is settled, a "send payout" message (m1) is put on a message queue. A
consumer process (w1) receives messages from the queue and, for each one, performs the payout by
crediting the amount to the seller's wallet balance, which is stored in the payments database (a
credit, once committed, is not reversed automatically), then acknowledges the message so the queue
deletes it.

The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A received message is hidden from consumers; if it is
not acknowledged within 7 clock ticks of being received (the visibility timeout) it becomes visible
again and will be delivered again. The consumer process can crash at any moment and is restarted
automatically, after which it continues receiving messages.

Processing and deduplication. The consumer keeps the ids of messages it has already paid out in a
set in its process memory. Before performing a payout it checks the set: if the id is there it skips
the payout and only acknowledges the message; otherwise it credits the wallet, adds the id to the
set, and acknowledges.

Initially m1 is in the queue and visible, nothing has been paid out, and w1 is idle.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl

  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types message consumer tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts: exactly one deduplication mode holds ---
    (dedup-none)      ; the consumer processes every delivery
    (dedup-durable)   ; processed ids are recorded in the database, atomically with the side effect
    (dedup-memory)    ; processed ids are recorded in an in-memory set of the consumer process
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (visibility-timeout ?t - tick)        ; age at which an unacknowledged message becomes visible again
    ;; --- queue ---
    (in-queue ?m - message) (visible ?m - message) (hidden ?m - message ?t - tick) (acked ?m - message)
    ;; --- consumer ---
    (idle ?w - consumer) (working ?w - consumer ?m - message) (handled ?w - consumer ?m - message)
    ;; --- effects of processing ---
    (unprocessed ?m - message) (processed ?m - message) (processed-twice ?m - message)
    (not-seen ?m - message) (seen ?m - message))

  (:action receive
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?w) (visible ?m) (in-queue ?m) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?w)) (not (visible ?m)) (working ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t)))
  (:action process-without-dedup
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-none) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-and-record-durably
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-durable) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)

  (:action process-and-record-in-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (working ?w ?m) (unprocessed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (not (unprocessed ?m)) (not (not-seen ?m)) (seen ?m)
                 (processed ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action skip-duplicate
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (handled ?w ?m)))
  (:action process-again
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (working ?w ?m) (processed ?m) (not-seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (working ?w ?m)) (processed-twice ?m) (handled ?w ?m)))

    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (handled ?w ?m) (hidden ?m ?t))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (not (in-queue ?m)) (idle ?w) (acked ?m)))

    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (hidden ?m ?u)))
  (:action reappear
    :parameters (?m - message ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (hidden ?m ?t) (visibility-timeout ?t) (in-queue ?m))
    :effect (and (not (hidden ?m ?t)) (visible ?m)))
  (:action crash-restart
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (handled ?w ?m)
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (idle ?w)))
  (:action crash-restart-losing-memory
    :parameters (?w - consumer ?m - message)
    :precondition (and (dedup-memory) (handled ?w ?m) (seen ?m))
    :effect (and (not (handled ?w ?m)) (not (seen ?m)) (not-seen ?m) (idle ?w))))
```

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".

completion.text:
**Yes. The payout for m1 can be performed twice.** The consumer stores the ids of messages it has already paid out only in process memory. If w1 crashes after crediting the wallet but before acknowledging m1, the restart wipes that memory. The credit stays committed in the database. After 7 ticks the queue redelivers m1, and the restarted w1 has no record of it, so it pays out again.

**Event sequence**

1. `(receive w1 m1 t0)`: w1 is idle and m1 is visible and in the queue. m1 becomes hidden at age t0, and w1 is working on it.
2. `(process-and-record-in-memory w1 m1)`: the mode is dedup-memory, and m1 is unprocessed and not seen. The wallet is credited, so m1 is processed, and its id goes into the in-memory set.
3. `(crash-restart-losing-memory w1 m1)`: w1 has handled m1 but has not acknowledged it. The crash clears the in-memory set, so m1 is no longer seen. w1 restarts and is idle. m1 stays hidden and in the queue, and the credit is not reversed.
4. `(tick m1 t0 t1)` through `(tick m1 t6 t7)`: m1 ages to t7 with no acknowledgement.
5. `(reappear m1 t7)`: t7 is the visibility timeout, so m1 becomes visible again.
6. `(receive w1 m1 t0)`: w1 is idle and m1 is visible, so w1 receives m1 again.
7. `(process-again w1 m1)`: w1 is working on m1, m1 is already processed, and m1 is not seen. The wallet is credited a second time, so `(processed-twice m1)` holds.

**Root cause and fix.** The record of which messages were paid out does not survive a crash, but the credit does. The fix is to store processed ids in the payments database, in the same transaction as the wallet credit. This is the model's `dedup-durable` mode, implemented for example as a unique-keyed table of payout ids. A redelivered message then fails the dedup check even after a crash.


```python
    """Return True if `n` is a prime number (an integer greater than 1 whose only
    positive divisors are 1 and itself), and False otherwise.
```

```python
    """Return a new list equal to `xs` rotated left by `k` positions: the element at
```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider handles requests one at a time,
in whatever order they arrive.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t1 (1 tick after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging. The provider treats every request it receives as a new payment: it approves the request
and charges the customer's card, then sends a success response. Requests carry the order number for
bookkeeping only; the provider does not use it to detect repeats.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain payments)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types order attempt tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-1)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---
    (approved ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; provider accepted attempt ?a and will charge it
    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet
    (record ?o - order)                 ; idempotency record for ?o stored
    (uncharged ?o - order)
    (charged ?o - order)                ; card charged once
    (charged-twice ?o - order))         ; card charged a second time (the violation)

  (:action send
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (ready ?o ?a) (first-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (ready ?o ?a)) (waiting ?o ?a) (in-flight ?o ?a) (clock ?o ?t)))
  (:action lose-request
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (in-flight ?o ?a)
    :effect (not (in-flight ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-2
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (in-flight ?o ?a))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-1
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-3) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (not (no-record ?o)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action accept-3
    :parameters (?o - order ?a - attempt)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (in-flight ?o ?a) (no-record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (approved ?o ?a)))
  (:action replay-2

    :precondition (and (mode-3) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))

    :precondition (and (mode-2) (in-flight ?o ?a) (record ?o))
    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))

    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
    :effect (and (not (approved ?o ?a)) (not (uncharged ?o)) (not (no-record ?o))

  (:action charge-again

    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (charged ?o))

  (:action receive-response
```

Question: Can the customer's card be charged twice for order o1? In the event model this means reaching a state where (charged-twice o1) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".

completion.text:
**Yes, the card can be charged twice for order o1.**

The provider treats every request it receives as a new payment and never checks the order number for repeats. In the event model this is `mode-1`, where `accept-2` approves any in-flight request with no idempotency check.

**How it happens:** The first request a0 is only delayed, not lost. The client times out and retries with a1. Both requests then reach the provider, and each one is approved and charged.

**Event sequence:**

1. `(send o1 a0 t0)`: The client sends a0. The request is in flight, the client is waiting, and the timer is at t0.
2. `(tick o1 a0 t0 t1)`: The timer reaches t1 with no response, because a0 is delayed in the network.
3. `(time-out-and-retry o1 a0 a1 t1)`: The client gives up on a0 and gets ready to send a1. The a0 request is still in flight.
4. `(send o1 a1 t0)`: The client sends retry a1.
5. `(accept-2 o1 a0)`: The delayed a0 arrives, and the provider approves it.
6. `(charge o1 a0)`: The card is charged once, which sets `charged o1`.
7. `(accept-2 o1 a1)`: a1 arrives, and the provider approves it as a new payment.
8. `(charge-again o1 a1)`: The card is charged a second time, which sets `charged-twice o1`.

**Root cause:** The provider has no idempotency key, and the client's timeout cannot tell a lost request from a slow one. Any retry while an earlier attempt is still in flight can produce a duplicate charge.

**Fix:** The provider should store an idempotency record keyed by order (or by idempotency key) when it accepts a request. Any later request for that order should replay the stored response instead of charging again (the `accept-1`/`replay-2` behaviour). The check and the reservation must happen together in one step, as `accept-1` does. If they are separate, as in `accept-3`, two concurrent requests can both see "no record" and both be charged.

```json

```

prompt:
--- Design document ---
Report-generation job: leader lock design (design doc)

Two worker processes, c1 and c2, may both try to run the nightly job, which overwrites a shared file
in object storage. To make sure only one of them writes, a worker must first acquire a lock from the
lock service. The lock is a lease: it is granted for 1 clock tick, after which the lock service
considers it expired and may grant it to the other worker. Each grant comes with a token from a
counter (k1 for the first grant, then k2, ...; k0 is the initial counter value and is never handed
out). Each worker writes the file at most once.

Workers can stall at any point for an unbounded time (garbage-collection pauses, VM migration,
slow network), and they learn nothing about lease expiry while stalled: a worker that has acquired
the lock keeps believing it holds it.

Writing. Right before writing, the worker asks the lock service whether it still holds an unexpired
lease, and writes only if the answer is yes. Every write carries the worker's token, and the storage
service remembers the highest token it has accepted: it rejects any write whose token is lower than
that (fencing), and accepts and records the others.

Initially the lock is free, no token has been issued yet (the counter is at k0), the storage has seen token k0, and neither worker has acquired the lock.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain lease-lock)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types client tick token)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick) (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (lease-limit ?t - tick)              ; lease age at which the lock service expires the lease
    (next-token ?k ?l - token)           ; token ?l is issued after ?k
    (token-less ?k ?l - token)           ; ?k < ?l
    (token-leq ?k ?l - token)            ; ?k <= ?l
    ;; --- lock service ---
    (lock-free) (holder ?c - client) (lease-age ?t - tick) (last-issued ?k - token)
    ;; --- clients ---
    (idle ?c - client)                   ; has not acquired the lock yet
    (believes ?c - client)               ; client thinks it holds the lock
    (lease-expired ?c - client)          ; the service expired this client's lease
    (token-of ?c - client ?k - token)
    (may-write ?c - client)              ; client is about to write to storage
    ;; --- storage ---
    (max-seen ?k - token)
    (wrote ?k - token)                   ; a write with token ?k was applied
    (corrupted))                         ; an older holder's write was applied after a newer holder's write

  (:action acquire
    :parameters (?c - client ?k ?l - token ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (idle ?c) (lock-free) (last-issued ?k) (next-token ?k ?l) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (idle ?c)) (not (lock-free)) (not (last-issued ?k)) (last-issued ?l)
                 (holder ?c) (believes ?c) (token-of ?c ?l) (lease-age ?t)))
```

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t11 (11 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

the lock keeps believing it holds it.

lease, and writes only if the answer is yes; if the lease has expired it abandons the job. The

Product page cache (design doc)

Product details live in a database and are cached in a key-value cache using the cache-aside

One writer process applies a batch of 8 price updates to the product, one after another, moving

can be delayed for any amount of time between reading the database and storing into the cache.
Cache entries have no expiry time.

Writes. For each update the writer first writes the new version to the database and then deletes
the product's cache entry, so the next read misses and loads the new version. The reader always
stores the value it read after a miss.

Initially the database holds v0, the cache is empty, the reader is idle, and the writer is about to start its first update.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain cache-aside)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types version)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (update-then-delete)   ; the writer updates the database, then deletes the cache entry
    (delete-then-update)   ; the writer deletes the cache entry, then updates the database
    (plain-set)            ; a reader that missed always stores the value it read
    (leased-set)           ; a reader may store its value only if its lease was not revoked by a delete
    ;; --- static ---
    (next-version ?v ?w - version) (older ?v ?w - version) (final-version ?v - version)
    ;; --- state ---
    (db ?v - version) (cache ?v - version) (cache-empty)
    (reader-idle) (reader-has ?v - version) (lease)
    (writer-start ?v - version)        ; writer is about to begin its updates (database at ?v)
    (writer-update ?v - version)       ; writer's next step: write the version after ?v to the database
    (writer-invalidate ?v - version)   ; writer's next step: delete the cache entry (database is at ?v)
    (writer-done)
    (stale))                           ; after the writer finished, the cache holds an older version than the database

    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (reader-idle) (cache-empty) (db ?v))
    :effect (and (not (reader-idle)) (reader-has ?v) (lease)))
  (:action fill-cache
    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (plain-set) (reader-has ?v) (cache-empty))
    :effect (and (not (reader-has ?v)) (not (cache-empty)) (cache ?v) (reader-idle)))

    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (leased-set) (reader-has ?v) (cache-empty) (lease))
    :effect (and (not (reader-has ?v)) (not (cache-empty)) (not (lease)) (cache ?v) (reader-idle)))

    :effect (and (not (writer-start ?v)) (writer-update ?v)))

    :parameters (?v - version)
    :precondition (and (delete-then-update) (writer-start ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-start ?v)) (writer-invalidate ?v)))

    :parameters (?v ?w - version)
    :precondition (and (writer-update ?v) (db ?v) (next-version ?v ?w))
    :effect (and (not (writer-update ?v)) (not (db ?v)) (db ?w) (writer-invalidate ?w)))

    :effect (and (not (writer-update ?v)) (writer-done)))

    :precondition (and (delete-then-update) (writer-invalidate ?v) (final-version ?v))
    :effect (and (not (writer-invalidate ?v)) (writer-done)))
```

Object names: versions v0 (initial) to v8.

Question: Can the cache be left holding an older version than the database after the writer has finished all its updates? In the event model this means reaching a state where (stale) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

End your answer with a JSON object in a ```json block, either
{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or
{"verdict": "safe"}

completion.text:
**Yes, it can happen.** The design is the classic cache-aside race: update the database, then delete the cache entry, with an unconditional fill. A reader can read an old value before an update and store it after that update's delete. Nothing removes the stale entry afterwards, because entries never expire.

**Assumptions about the static facts.** The model's static facts aren't listed, so I assume the obvious ones: `next-version` chains v0 to v8 in order, `final-version v8` holds, and `older v7 v8` holds. The design facts in force are `update-then-delete` and `plain-set`.

**Event sequence:**

1. **Writer applies updates 1 to 7.** It runs `begin-update-first v0`, then for each update a `write-db` followed by `invalidate-empty`, bringing the database to v7. The cache stays empty throughout, so the reader is still idle.
2. **Reader misses.** `read-miss v7`: the cache is empty and the database holds v7, so the reader now holds v7.
3. **Writer applies update 8.**
   - `write-db v7 v8`: the database now holds v8.
   - `invalidate-empty v8`: the cache is already empty. This deletes nothing useful; it only revokes a lease, which plain-set ignores.
   - `finish-after-delete v8`: the writer is done.
4. **Delayed reader fills the cache.** `fill-cache v7`: the cache is still empty, so the reader stores v7.
5. **Stale state reached.** `observe-stale v7 v8`: the cache holds v7 and the database holds v8.

**Root cause:** the delete can land between the reader's database read and its cache store. Possible fixes:
- Leased or conditional set, which is the `leased-set` design fact. The delete revokes the lease, so the late fill is rejected.
- A delayed second delete.
- A TTL on cache entries.


```python
def bulk_price(unit_cents, qty):
    """Return the price in cents of `qty` items costing `unit_cents` each. The gross
    price is unit_cents * qty. Orders of 100 or more items get 15% off and orders of
    50 to 99 items get 10% off; the discount amount is rounded down to a whole number
    of cents and subtracted from the gross price.
    """
    gross = unit_cents * qty

    elif qty >= 50:
```

Yes, there is a bug: the 15% tier starts at 99 items instead of 100.

The docstring gives 15% off for orders of **100 or more** and 10% off for **50 to 99** items. The code tests `qty >= 99` for the 15% tier, so an order of exactly 99 items gets 15% off instead of 10%.

arbitrarily. A checkout first reserves a unit (a hold), then the customer pays to confirm the
purchase.

Holds are temporary: a hold that is not paid for expires after 3 clock ticks, and the unit goes
back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

Reserving. The checkout thread reserves with a single atomic conditional update
(UPDATE stock SET count = count - 1 WHERE count > 0); if no row is updated the customer is told the
item is sold out.

Paying. The payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active; payment
for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

Initially all customers are browsing and the stock count is 3.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
    (mode-4)
```

```pddl
  (:domain inventory)
  (:objects
    c1 c2 c3 c4 - customer
    q0 q1 q2 q3 - level
```

- **`(mode-4)` is true.** Reserving is a single atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE count > 0`. That is the atomic `reserve-1` event.

completion.text:
**Verdict: safe.** The cache cannot be left holding an older version than the database after the writer finishes.

**Which design facts apply**
- The writer writes the database first and then deletes the cache entry. So `mode-4` holds: `begin-1` moves to `writer-update`, and `finish-2` ends the writer after its last delete.
- The cache only accepts a store from a reader with a valid lease. So `mode-1` holds: `fill-2` is the only store action, and it requires `(lease)`.

**Why `(stale)` cannot be reached**

1. **Where a lease comes from.** The only action that grants `(lease)` is `read-miss`. It needs `(reader-idle)` and records whatever version the database holds at that moment.

2. **What a delete does.** Both `invalidate` and `invalidate-empty` remove `(lease)`. `invalidate` also clears any cached value.

3. **The last delete.** The final write is `write-db v3 v4`. After it, the writer's next step is a delete with the database at v4. That delete empties the cache, and any value cached earlier is gone.

4. **A reader holding an old value at that delete.** Suppose the reader holds a version read before `write-db v3 v4`, so v3 or older. The last delete revokes its lease. The reader cannot get a new lease while still holding that value, because `read-miss` requires it to be idle first. Its only options are `abandon-fill`, or `fill-2`, which is now blocked.

5. **Any lease granted after `write-db v3 v4`.** Such a lease comes from a `read-miss` that read the database, which by then holds v4. The only possible store is therefore v4, whether it happens before or after `finish-2`.

6. **Conclusion.** After the writer finishes, the cache is either empty or holds v4. `observe-stale` needs a cached version older than the database's v4, so it can never fire.

Lease revocation on every delete, together with the reader holding only one read at a time, closes the classic cache-aside race where a slow reader stores an old value after the delete.

completion.text:
**Verdict: violation.** The payout for m1 can be performed twice.

**Which mode applies.** The design says the consumer "performs the payout for every message it receives, then acknowledges it." It never checks whether a message was already handled. That matches `mode-3`, whose `process-2` action has no `seen`/`not-seen` guard. Initially m1 is `in-queue`, `visible`, `unprocessed` and `not-seen`, and w1 is `idle`.

**Failure scenario.** The consumer can crash after the bank call but before the acknowledgement:

1. `(receive w1 m1 t0)`: w1 takes m1, and m1 is hidden at age t0.
2. `(process-2 w1 m1)`: the bank payout is made, so m1 is `processed`. m1 is still `not-seen`, because `process-2` never marks it.
3. `(crash-restart w1 m1)`: w1 crashes before `ack` and restarts idle. m1 stays in the queue, still hidden.
4. `(tick m1 t0 t1)` through `(tick m1 t4 t5)`: the visibility timeout runs out.
5. `(reappear m1 t5)`: m1 is visible again, since `visibility-timeout t5` holds and m1 is still `in-queue`.
6. `(receive w1 m1 t0)`: w1 is idle, and m1 is visible and in the queue.
7. `(process-again w1 m1)`: m1 is `processed` and `not-seen`, so the payout happens a second time and `(processed-twice m1)` holds.

**Root cause.** At-least-once delivery combined with a non-idempotent side effect and no deduplication. A crash between "pay" and "ack" always leads to redelivery and a second payout.

**Fix.** Make the payout idempotent. For example, pass a stable idempotency key (the message ID) to the bank API, or durably record the message as paid in the same transaction as the side effect and skip messages that are already recorded. The dedup record must survive crashes; the `crash-1` and `mode-1` variant shows that a record lost on crash is not enough.

--- Design document ---
Checkout payment flow (design doc)

When a customer places order o1, the checkout service (the client) sends a charge request to an
external payment provider and waits for the reply. The network between them is unreliable: a request
or a response can be lost, and messages can be delayed arbitrarily, so a request may still be in
transit after the client has stopped waiting for it. The provider serves requests concurrently on
several worker threads, in whatever order they arrive, so the steps of different requests (looking up
records, charging, writing records) can interleave.

Each request is one attempt (a0 for the first try). After sending an attempt the client starts a
timer at t0; every clock tick advances it by one, and when it reaches t15 (15 ticks after sending)
without a response the client gives up on that attempt and retries with the next attempt number
(a1, then a2). At most two retries are made. If a success response arrives while the client is still
waiting, the order is confirmed and no further attempts are made.

Charging and duplicate protection. Every attempt for an order carries the same idempotency key
(derived from the order number). When a request arrives, the provider looks the key up and, in the
same atomic database operation, inserts a reservation if it is absent (an insert-if-absent with a
unique constraint). Only a request whose insert succeeded is approved and charged; when the charge
succeeds the reservation is completed with the stored response. A request whose key already has a
completed record gets the stored success response back without a new charge; a request that finds
only an unfinished reservation is not charged either.

Initially the client is about to send attempt a0 for order o1; nothing has been charged and the provider has no record for o1.

is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state

```pddl
    (dedup-none)     ; the provider does not deduplicate requests
    (dedup-atomic)   ; the provider looks up and reserves the idempotency key in one atomic step
    (dedup-racy)     ; the provider looks up the key, but only records it after the charge succeeds
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-attempt ?a ?b - attempt)   ; attempt ?b is the retry that follows attempt ?a
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)         ; timer value ?u follows ?t
    (first-tick ?t - tick)           ; timer value right after a request is sent
    (timeout-tick ?t - tick)         ; timer value at which the client gives up waiting
    ;; --- client ---
    (ready ?o - order ?a - attempt)    ; client is about to send attempt ?a for order ?o
    (waiting ?o - order ?a - attempt)  ; client sent attempt ?a and awaits the response
    (clock ?o - order ?t - tick)       ; client's timer for the outstanding attempt
    (confirmed ?o - order)             ; client received a success response
    ;; --- network ---
    (in-flight ?o - order ?a - attempt) ; request of attempt ?a travelling to the provider
    (response ?o - order)               ; success response travelling back to the client
    ;; --- provider ---

    (no-record ?o - order)              ; no idempotency record (and no reservation) for ?o yet

    (uncharged ?o - order)

    :effect (and (not (in-flight ?o ?a)) (response ?o)))
  (:action charge

    :precondition (and (approved ?o ?a) (uncharged ?o))
```
